app.title: RNA · Metal-Ion Binding Predictor (RNA-GNN Streamlit demo)
app.summary: The interface loads a trained graph neural network and a bundled RNA structure. The structure has already been cut into candidate ion positions, each a small atomic graph. It scores every candidate, binarizes the scores at the threshold that maximizes Youden's J, and reports the number of candidates, the predicted sites, ROC AUC and the threshold. The predicted positions are written back into the structure file as heteroatoms. The person then rotates and zooms the experimental structure and the predicted one side by side, to see whether the predicted ions sit where the crystal ions do.

task.text: Check where a trained graph model predicts metal ions bind in an RNA structure, against the ions seen experimentally.

data.text: An RNA 3D structure broken into candidate ion positions, each a local atomic graph with a known binding label, plus a trained model checkpoint
data.item: a candidate ion position in an RNA structure, represented as a small graph of nearby atoms

stage.text: checking a trained model's binding-site predictions against an experimental structure, after training

mechanism.text: Model inference and threshold selection run on load and fill a row of readout metrics. The thresholded positions are merged into a structure file, which is shown in a 3D viewer beside the original experimental structure so the two can be compared.

field.text: graph neural network prediction of metal-ion binding sites in RNA structural biology

workflow.name: score candidates with a trained model and compare the predictions to known positives

steps.here: The trained GCN checkpoint and the structure's pickled candidate-site graphs are loaded once and cached across reruns. The sidebar shows the architecture and the compute device.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Every candidate graph is scored. A threshold is chosen by maximizing Youden's J on the ROC curve, and ROC AUC is computed against the experimental labels.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Four metric cards report the number of candidate sites, the predicted ion sites, ROC AUC and the chosen threshold. An expander explains how the candidate graphs are built.
The coordinates of the positive predictions are parsed and written as HETATM records into a merged PDB file.
Two Mol* viewers show the experimental structure with its crystal ions and the structure with predicted Mg²⁺ sites. Each can be rotated and zoomed, under a colour legend.

distinctive: Each candidate is a local atomic graph around a grid position, scored by a graph convolutional network with mean pooling
The decision threshold is chosen automatically by Youden's J, to favour recall under heavy class imbalance
Predictions are written back into the structure file as heteroatoms, so they can be inspected in 3D next to the experimental ions
Model and graph loading are cached, so reruns are instant
